source.text: Ἔλεγεν δὲ παραβολὴν αὐτοῖς πρὸς τὸ δεῖν πάντοτε προσεύχεσθαι αὐτοὺς καὶ μὴ ἐγκακεῖν, λέγων· Κριτής τις ἦν ἔν τινι πόλει τὸν θεὸν μὴ φοβούμενος καὶ ἄνθρωπον μὴ ἐντρεπόμενος.

records.literal_gloss: He was speaking then a parable to them about the [need] for them always to pray and not to lose heart, \v 2 saying, A certain judge there was in a certain city, God not fearing and man not respecting.

en.L: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was telling them a parable about their need always to pray and not to lose heart, \v 2 saying, "In a certain city there was a certain judge who did not fear God and did not respect {{gender:people|man}}.
en.B: Jesus told them a parable about their need to pray at all times and not lose heart. \v 2 He said, "There was once a judge in a certain city who did not fear God and had no regard for anyone.
en.R: Jesus told {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} disciples a story. He wanted to teach them that they should always pray and never give up hope. \v 2 He said, "In a certain town there was a judge. He had no fear of God, and he did not care about people.

es.L: Y les decía una parábola sobre la necesidad de que ellos oraran siempre y no se desanimaran, \v 2 diciendo: «En cierta ciudad había un juez que no temía a Dios ni sentía respeto por {{gender:ninguna persona|ningún hombre}}.
es.B: Jesús les contó una parábola para enseñarles que debían orar en todo tiempo y no desanimarse. \v 2 Les dijo: «Había una vez, en cierta ciudad, un juez que no temía a Dios ni tenía consideración por nadie.
es.R: Jesús les contó una historia a {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} discípulos. Quería enseñarles que siempre debían orar y nunca perder la esperanza. \v 2 Les dijo: «En cierto pueblo había un juez. No tenía temor de Dios, y no le importaba la gente.

fr.L: Et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} leur disait une parabole [pour montrer] qu’il leur fallait toujours prier et ne pas perdre courage, \v 2 en disant : « Il y avait dans une certaine ville un certain juge qui ne craignait pas Dieu et n’avait pas d’égards pour {{gender:les gens|les hommes}}.
fr.B: Jésus leur dit une parabole pour leur montrer qu’ils devaient prier en tout temps sans se décourager. \v 2 Il dit : « Il y avait une fois, dans une ville, un juge qui ne craignait pas Dieu et n’avait d’égards pour personne.
fr.R: Jésus a raconté une histoire à {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} disciples. Il voulait leur apprendre qu’ils devaient toujours prier, sans jamais perdre espoir. \v 2 Il a dit : « Dans une ville, il y avait un juge. Il ne craignait pas Dieu, et il ne se souciait pas des gens.

sw.L: Naye alikuwa akiwaambia mfano kuhusu wao kuhitaji kuomba siku zote na kutokata tamaa, \v 2 akisema, "Katika mji fulani palikuwa na hakimu fulani asiyemcha Mungu wala kumheshimu mwanadamu.
sw.B: Yesu aliwaambia mfano kuhusu jinsi wanavyopaswa kuomba wakati wote bila kukata tamaa. \v 2 Akasema, "Katika mji mmoja kulikuwa na hakimu ambaye hakumwogopa Mungu, wala hakumheshimu mtu yeyote.
sw.R: Yesu aliwaambia wanafunzi {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} mfano. Alitaka kuwafundisha kwamba wanapaswa kuomba siku zote, wala wasikate tamaa. \v 2 Akasema, "Katika mji fulani kulikuwa na hakimu. Hakumwogopa Mungu, na hakuwajali watu.

decisions.choice: about their need always to pray: Luke states the point of the parable before it is told
alternatives: a title for the story only
decisions.reason: Luke tells the reader in advance what the parable teaches: to keep on praying and not give up while waiting for God to act (18:7-8).

decisions.choice: lose heart: become discouraged and give up
decisions.reason: The verb means to grow weary or lose courage (2 Corinthians 4:1, 16).

decisions.choice: did not fear God and did not respect people: answerable to no one
decisions.reason: To fear God and respect people was the mark of a just judge (2 Chronicles 19:6-7). This judge cared for neither.

decisions.choice: his disciples
decisions.reason: Readable says who "them" are; Jesus has been speaking to the disciples since 17:22.

decisions.choice: the quotation opens here and runs to 18:5
alternatives: a quotation for each part of the story
decisions.reason: The parable is one speech; the Lord's comment in 18:6 starts a new one.

decisions.choice: parábola (L, B); historia (R)
decisions.reason: The word used for Jesus' parables across the New Testament drafts; Readable says "historia", as the English Readable says "story". The same in verse 9.

decisions.choice: {{gender:ninguna persona|ningún hombre}}
decisions.reason: As the English Literal {{gender:people|man}}: the Greek word means a human being (meaning decision m3), and Spanish can say it either way; the span takes in the whole phrase that agrees. Balanced says "nadie" and Readable "la gente", which need no span. The same in verses 4, 11 and 27.

decisions.choice: narration in the passé simple (L, B) and the passé composé (R); the parables told by Jesus in the passé composé at every level
decisions.reason: As in Luke 2, 4 and 17: the passé simple is the normal tense of written narrative, and Readable uses the passé composé throughout. The parables of the judge and of the Pharisee and the tax collector are Jesus's speech, so they keep the tenses of speech ("il n’a pas voulu", "ils sont montés"), as the style guide asks. This holds for the whole chapter.

decisions.choice: {{gender:les gens|les hommes}} (L); n’avait d’égards pour personne (B); ne se souciait pas des gens (R)
decisions.reason: The word means people in general (m3). Literal keeps a noun, so it carries the setting, as in English; Balanced and Readable use "personne" and "les gens", which are already inclusive and need no span. The same in 18:4.

decisions.choice: mfano (every level)
decisions.reason: The word used for Jesus' parables across the New Testament drafts, at every level, even where the English Readable says "story". The same in verse 9.

decisions.choice: wanafunzi {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}}; no span on verb prefixes
decisions.reason: As through Luke, Swahili spans go only on free pronouns and possessives, never on verb prefixes (alikuwa, akasema), which cannot take a capital; so Swahili has fewer spans than English in this chapter.

source.text: χήρα δὲ ἦν ἐν τῇ πόλει ἐκείνῃ καὶ ἤρχετο πρὸς αὐτὸν λέγουσα· Ἐκδίκησόν με ἀπὸ τοῦ ἀντιδίκου μου.

records.literal_gloss: A widow then there was in the city that, and she was coming to him saying, Avenge me of the adversary of me.

en.L: And there was a widow in that city, and she kept coming to him, saying, 'Give me justice against my adversary.'
en.B: In that city there was also a widow who came to him again and again. She said, 'Give me my rights against my opponent.'
en.R: In that town there was also a widow. She kept coming to the judge and saying, 'Someone is treating me unfairly. Please judge my case and give me justice.'

es.L: Y había en esa ciudad una viuda, y seguía viniendo a él y le decía: “Hazme justicia frente a mi adversario”.
es.B: En esa misma ciudad había también una viuda que acudía a él una y otra vez. Le decía: “Defiende mi derecho frente a mi contrario”.
es.R: En ese pueblo había también una viuda. Iba una y otra vez a ver al juez y le decía: “Alguien me está tratando injustamente. Por favor, juzga mi caso y hazme justicia”.

fr.L: Et il y avait dans cette ville-là une veuve, et elle venait à lui, en disant : “Fais-moi justice contre mon adversaire.”
fr.B: Dans cette même ville, il y avait aussi une veuve qui venait le trouver sans cesse. Elle lui disait : “Rends-moi justice contre mon adversaire.”
fr.R: Dans cette ville, il y avait aussi une veuve. Elle venait sans arrêt voir le juge et elle lui disait : “Quelqu’un me traite injustement. S’il te plaît, juge mon affaire et rends-moi justice.”

sw.L: Na palikuwa na mjane katika mji ule, naye alikuwa akija kwake, akisema, 'Nitendee haki dhidi ya mpinzani wangu.'
sw.B: Katika mji huo pia palikuwa na mjane aliyemwendea tena na tena, akisema, 'Uamue kesi yangu kwa haki dhidi ya mpinzani wangu.'
sw.R: Katika mji huo pia kulikuwa na mjane mmoja. Aliendelea kumwendea yule hakimu, akisema, 'Mtu fulani ananitendea isivyo haki. Tafadhali sikiliza kesi yangu na unipatie haki.'

decisions.choice: a widow: a woman with no husband to support or defend her
decisions.reason: A widow often had no one to speak for her in court. The law commanded special care for widows (Exodus 22:22; Deuteronomy 10:18), and the prophets condemned judges who ignored them (Isaiah 1:23).

decisions.choice: give me justice: decide my case in my favor and make it right
decisions.reason: The verb can mean to avenge, but in a court case it means to see that justice is done for someone who has been wronged.

decisions.choice: she kept coming: again and again
decisions.reason: The tense shows repeated action, which is the point of the story.

decisions.choice: Someone is treating me unfairly. Please judge my case
alternatives: Give me justice against my adversary
decisions.reason: Readable explains what kind of help she asked for.

decisions.choice: Hazme justicia (L, R); Defiende mi derecho (B)
decisions.reason: The literal gloss says "avenge", but the widow asks the judge to decide her case in her favour and set it right (meaning decision m2), not to take revenge. "Hacer justicia" says that; the same in verses 5, 7 and 8.

decisions.choice: nitendee haki (L); uamue kesi yangu kwa haki (B); unipatie haki (R)
decisions.reason: The literal gloss says "avenge", but the widow asks the judge to decide her case in her favour and set it right (meaning decision m2), not to take revenge. "Haki" here is justice in a court, which Swahili names with the same word as righteousness; the same in verses 5, 7 and 8.

source.text: καὶ οὐκ ἤθελεν ἐπὶ χρόνον, μετὰ ταῦτα δὲ εἶπεν ἐν ἑαυτῷ· Εἰ καὶ τὸν θεὸν οὐ φοβοῦμαι οὐδὲ ἄνθρωπον ἐντρέπομαι, διά γε τὸ παρέχειν μοι κόπον τὴν χήραν ταύτην ἐκδικήσω αὐτήν ἵνα μὴ εἰς τέλος ἐρχομένη ὑπωπιάζῃ με.

records.literal_gloss: And not he would for a time; afterward however he said within himself, If even God not I fear nor man respect, \v 5 because yet causes me trouble the widow this, I will avenge her, so that not to the end coming she exhaust me.

en.L: And for a time he was not willing; but afterward he said within himself, 'Even though I do not fear God nor respect {{gender:people|man}}, \v 5 yet because this widow causes me trouble, I will give her justice, so that she does not keep coming and in the end wear me out.'"
en.B: For a while he refused. But later he said to himself, 'I do not fear God and I have no regard for anyone. \v 5 Still, this widow is such a nuisance that I will give her justice. If I do not, she will keep coming until she wears me out.'"
en.R: For a while the judge refused to help her. But at last he said to himself, 'I do not fear God, and I do not care about people. \v 5 But this widow keeps bothering me. So I will make sure she gets justice. If I do not, she will keep coming back and wear me out!'"

es.L: Y durante un tiempo no quiso, pero después dijo dentro de sí: “Aunque no temo a Dios ni siento respeto por {{gender:ninguna persona|ningún hombre}}, \v 5 como esta viuda me da trabajo, le haré justicia, para que no siga viniendo hasta acabar agotándome”».
es.B: Durante un tiempo se negó. Pero más tarde se dijo: “Yo no temo a Dios ni tengo consideración por nadie. \v 5 Aun así, esta viuda es tan molesta que le haré justicia. Si no, seguirá viniendo hasta dejarme agotado”».
es.R: Por un tiempo el juez no quiso ayudarla. Pero al final se dijo: “Yo no tengo temor de Dios, y no me importa la gente. \v 5 Pero esta viuda no deja de molestarme. Así que me encargaré de que se le haga justicia. ¡Si no, seguirá viniendo y me dejará agotado!”».

fr.L: Et pendant un temps il n’a pas voulu ; mais ensuite il s’est dit en lui-même : “Même si je ne crains pas Dieu et ne respecte pas {{gender:les gens|les hommes}}, \v 5 pourtant, parce que cette veuve me cause du tracas, je lui ferai justice, afin qu’elle ne finisse pas par venir m’épuiser.” »
fr.B: Pendant un certain temps, il a refusé. Mais ensuite il s’est dit : “Je ne crains pas Dieu et je n’ai d’égards pour personne. \v 5 Pourtant, cette veuve m’importune tellement que je vais lui rendre justice. Sinon, elle va continuer à venir jusqu’à m’épuiser.” »
fr.R: Pendant un moment, le juge n’a pas voulu l’aider. Mais finalement, il s’est dit : “Je ne crains pas Dieu, et je ne me soucie pas des gens. \v 5 Mais cette veuve n’arrête pas de m’embêter. Alors je vais faire en sorte qu’elle obtienne justice. Sinon, elle va revenir encore et encore, et elle va m’épuiser !” »

sw.L: Naye kwa muda hakutaka; lakini baadaye akasema moyoni mwake, 'Ingawa simwogopi Mungu wala simheshimu mwanadamu, \v 5 lakini kwa kuwa mjane huyu ananiletea taabu, nitamtendea haki, asije akaendelea kuja hadi mwisho akanichosha kabisa.'"
sw.B: Kwa muda alikataa. Lakini baadaye alijisemea, 'Mimi simwogopi Mungu, wala simjali mtu yeyote. \v 5 Hata hivyo, mjane huyu ananiudhi mno, kwa hiyo nitamtendea haki. La sivyo, ataendelea kuja mpaka anichoshe kabisa.'"
sw.R: Kwa muda yule hakimu alikataa kumsaidia. Lakini mwishowe akajisemea, 'Mimi simwogopi Mungu, wala siwajali watu. \v 5 Lakini mjane huyu anaendelea kunisumbua. Kwa hiyo nitahakikisha anapata haki yake. La sivyo, ataendelea kurudi na kunichosha!'"

decisions.choice: wear me out: exhaust me with her pestering
decisions.reason: The verb first meant to strike under the eye, as a boxer does (1 Corinthians 9:27). Here it is probably used loosely, of being worn down; the judge is tired, not afraid of being hit. Some take it to mean that she will damage his reputation.

decisions.choice: to the end coming: by coming on and on, or coming at last
decisions.reason: The phrase can mean "in the end" or "continually". Either way, the judge gives in because she will not stop.

decisions.choice: he said within himself: the judge's motive is his own comfort
alternatives: he came to care about her
decisions.reason: The judge does not change his character. Even a man like this gives in to persistence; the next verses argue from the lesser to the greater (18:7).

decisions.choice: the quotation closes here
decisions.reason: The narrator speaks in 18:6.

decisions.choice: mwanadamu, with no gender span
decisions.reason: The English Literal has {{gender:people|man}} here and in verses 2, 11 and 27. "Mwanadamu" and "mtu" mean a human being, man or woman, so Swahili has no second wording for the setting to choose; the same for the reflexive verbs in verse 14.

source.text: εἶπεν δὲ ὁ κύριος· Ἀκούσατε τί ὁ κριτὴς τῆς ἀδικίας λέγει·

records.literal_gloss: Said then the Lord, Hear what the judge of unrighteousness says;

en.L: And the Lord said, "Hear what the unrighteous judge says.
en.B: The Lord said, "Listen to what the unjust judge says.
en.R: Then the Lord Jesus said, "Listen to what this unfair judge says.

es.L: Y dijo el Señor: «{{plural_you:Oigan|Oíd}} lo que dice el juez de la injusticia.
es.B: El Señor dijo: «{{plural_you:Escuchen|Escuchad}} lo que dice el juez injusto.
es.R: Entonces el Señor Jesús dijo: «{{plural_you:Escuchen|Escuchad}} lo que dice este juez injusto.

fr.L: Et le Seigneur dit : « Écoutez ce que dit le juge injuste.
fr.B: Le Seigneur dit : « Écoutez bien ce que dit ce juge injuste.
fr.R: Ensuite, le Seigneur Jésus a dit : « Écoutez ce que dit ce juge malhonnête.

sw.L: Naye Bwana akasema, "Sikieni asemavyo hakimu wa udhalimu.
sw.B: Bwana alisema, "Sikilizeni anachosema yule hakimu dhalimu.
sw.R: Kisha Bwana Yesu alisema, "Sikilizeni anachosema hakimu huyu asiyetenda haki.

decisions.choice: the Lord: Luke the narrator calls Jesus by his title
the judge of unrighteousness: the unjust judge
alternatives: a judge who rules on unrighteousness
decisions.reason: The Hebrew way of describing someone by a noun ("of unrighteousness") means a judge marked by injustice (16:8).

decisions.choice: the Lord Jesus
decisions.reason: Readable adds the name, as in 12:42.

decisions.choice: the quotation opens here and runs to 18:8
decisions.reason: The Lord's comment on the parable is one speech.

source.text: ὁ δὲ θεὸς οὐ μὴ ποιήσῃ τὴν ἐκδίκησιν τῶν ἐκλεκτῶν αὐτοῦ τῶν βοώντων αὐτῷ ἡμέρας καὶ νυκτός, καὶ μακροθυμεῖ ἐπ’ αὐτοῖς;

records.literal_gloss: And God not not shall execute the avenging of the elect of him, the [ones] crying out to him day and night, and is he delaying over them?

en.L: And will not God bring about justice for {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} chosen ones, who cry out to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} day and night? And will {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} delay over them?
en.B: Then surely God will give justice to the people {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has chosen, when they call out to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} day and night. Will {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} be slow to help them?
en.R: God will surely see that {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} chosen people get justice. They cry out to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} day and night. Will {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} keep them waiting?

es.L: Y Dios, ¿acaso no hará justicia a {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} elegidos, los que {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} gritan de día y de noche? ¿Y se demorará con ellos?
es.B: Entonces, sin duda Dios hará justicia a las personas que {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} ha escogido, cuando {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} claman de día y de noche. ¿Acaso tardará en ayudarlas?
es.R: Dios se encargará, sin duda, de que {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} pueblo escogido reciba justicia. Ellos {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} piden ayuda a gritos de día y de noche. ¿Los hará esperar?

fr.L: Et est-ce que Dieu ne fera pas justice à {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} élus, qui crient vers {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} jour et nuit ? Et tarde-t-{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} à leur égard ?
fr.B: Alors Dieu fera sûrement justice aux gens qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} a choisis, quand ils crient vers {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} jour et nuit. Tardera-t-{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} à les secourir ?
fr.R: Dieu fera sûrement en sorte que ceux qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} a choisis obtiennent justice. Ils crient vers {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} jour et nuit. Va-t-{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} les faire attendre ?

sw.L: Na Mungu, je, hatawatendea haki wateule {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}}, wale wanaomlilia mchana na usiku? Naye je, atawakawilia?
sw.B: Basi, hakika Mungu atawapatia hukumu ya haki watu {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} waliochaguliwa, wanapomlilia mchana na usiku. Je, atachelewa kuwasaidia?
sw.R: Hakika Mungu atahakikisha kwamba watu {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} waliochaguliwa wanapata haki. Wao humlilia mchana na usiku. Je, atawaacha wangoje?

decisions.choice: will not God bring about justice: a question expecting a strong "yes"
decisions.reason: The double negative expects "Yes, of course he will". If an unjust judge gives in, how much more will God, who is just and loves his people.

decisions.choice: his chosen ones: the people God has chosen as his own
alternatives: a small group of special believers
decisions.reason: Israel was God's chosen people (Isaiah 65:9); the word is used of all who belong to God (Romans 8:33).

decisions.choice: and will he delay over them: a second question, expecting "no"
alternatives: though he is patient with them
and he is patient with them
decisions.reason: The verb means to be patient or to be slow to act. Its sense here is debated. Taken as a question, it expects that God will not put them off; others read it as a statement that God is patient. 18:8 says he will act quickly.

decisions.choice: a statement: surely God will
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the expected answer as a statement.

decisions.choice: elegidos (L); las personas que él ha escogido (B); su pueblo escogido (R)
decisions.reason: The people God has chosen as his own (meaning decision m2). "Los elegidos" is the term used across the New Testament drafts; Balanced and Readable say it as a clause and as "his chosen people", as the English does.

decisions.choice: Et est-ce que Dieu ne fera pas justice … ? (L)
alternatives: Et Dieu ne fera-t-il pas justice … ?
decisions.reason: The usual French inversion repeats the subject as a pronoun ("Dieu ne fera-t-il pas"), which would need the deity_pronoun setting inside the inversion and read oddly with the capital. "Est-ce que" keeps the question expecting "yes" (m1) with the same meaning.

decisions.choice: wateule (L); watu wake waliochaguliwa (B, R)
decisions.reason: The people God has chosen as his own (meaning decision m2). "Wateule" is the term used across the New Testament drafts at Literal; Balanced and Readable say "his people who were chosen", which is plainer.

source.text: λέγω ὑμῖν ὅτι ποιήσει τὴν ἐκδίκησιν αὐτῶν ἐν τάχει.

records.literal_gloss: I say to you that he will execute the avenging of them in quickness.

en.L: I tell you that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will bring about justice for them quickly.
en.B: I tell you, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will see them vindicated, and without delay.
en.R: I tell you, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will give them justice, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will do it quickly.

es.L: {{plural_you:Les|Os}} digo que hará justicia por ellos con prontitud.
es.B: {{plural_you:Les|Os}} digo que les hará justicia, y sin tardanza.
es.R: {{plural_you:Les|Os}} digo que les hará justicia, y que lo hará pronto.

fr.L: Je vous dis qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} leur fera justice promptement.
fr.B: Je vous le dis, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} les rétablira dans leur droit, et sans tarder.
fr.R: Je vous le dis, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} leur rendra justice, et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} le fera vite.

sw.L: Nawaambia kwamba atawatendea haki upesi.
sw.B: Nawaambia, atawatendea haki, tena bila kukawia.
sw.R: Nawaambia, atawapa haki, {{deity_pronoun:naye|Naye}} atafanya hivyo upesi.

decisions.choice: quickly: soon, or suddenly when the time comes
decisions.reason: The phrase can mean soon or swiftly. Jesus has just spoken of days of waiting (17:22), so the point may be that when God acts he will not hold back.

decisions.choice: bring about justice: put right what has been done to them
decisions.reason: The same word as in 18:3, 5.

decisions.choice: see them vindicated
decisions.reason: Balanced uses a word for being shown to be in the right.

decisions.choice: hará, with no deity_pronoun span
decisions.reason: The English writes "he will" with a span on "he". Spanish leaves the subject inside the verb ("hará"), where it cannot take a capital, so there is no span there; free pronouns such as "él", "le" and "lo" keep theirs. So Spanish has fewer spans than English through this chapter.

source.text: πλὴν ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου ἐλθὼν ἆρα εὑρήσει τὴν πίστιν ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς;

records.literal_gloss: Nevertheless the Son of Man having come, indeed will he find the faith on the earth?

en.L: Nevertheless, when the Son of Man comes, will {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} find faith on the earth?"
en.B: Even so, when the Son of Man comes, will {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} find this kind of faith on the earth?"
en.R: But when the Son of Man comes, will {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} find anyone on earth who still has faith?"

es.L: Sin embargo, cuando venga el Hijo del Hombre, ¿encontrará de veras la fe sobre la tierra?».
es.B: Aun así, cuando venga el Hijo del Hombre, ¿encontrará esta clase de fe en la tierra?».
es.R: Pero cuando venga el Hijo del Hombre, ¿encontrará a alguien en la tierra que todavía tenga fe?».

fr.L: Toutefois, le Fils de l’homme, quand {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} viendra, trouvera-t-{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} la foi sur la terre ? »
fr.B: Mais quand le Fils de l’homme viendra, trouvera-t-{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} cette foi-là sur la terre ? »
fr.R: Mais quand le Fils de l’homme viendra, est-ce qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} trouvera encore sur la terre des gens qui ont la foi ? »

sw.B: Hata hivyo, Mwana wa Adamu atakapokuja, je, atakuta imani ya namna hii duniani?"
sw.R: Lakini Mwana wa Adamu atakapokuja, je, atamkuta mtu yeyote duniani ambaye bado ana imani?"

alternatives: the Christian faith as a body of teaching
decisions.reason: The word has the article, "the faith", which points back to the kind of faith the parable has shown (18:1).

decisions.choice: will he find: a question that warns, without giving the answer
alternatives: a prediction that no one will have faith

decisions.choice: this kind of faith (B); anyone ... who still has faith (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable show the article's point, as the meaning decision explains.

en.L: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} also told this parable to some who trusted in themselves that they were righteous and looked down on everyone else.
en.B: There were some who relied on themselves, sure that they were righteous, and who looked down on all others. Jesus told them this parable.
en.R: Some people felt sure that they were good and right with God, and they thought they were better than everyone else. Jesus told them this story.

es.L: Y dijo también a algunos que confiaban en sí mismos, en que eran justos, y que tenían por nada a los demás, esta parábola:
es.B: Había algunos que confiaban en sí mismos, seguros de ser justos, y miraban a todos los demás por encima del hombro. A ellos les contó Jesús esta parábola:
es.R: Algunas personas estaban seguras de que eran buenas y de que estaban bien con Dios, y se creían mejores que todos los demás. Jesús les contó esta historia:

fr.L: Et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} dit aussi cette parabole à certains qui se confiaient en eux-mêmes, [persuadés] qu’ils étaient justes, et qui méprisaient les autres.
fr.B: Il y avait des gens qui comptaient sur eux-mêmes, sûrs d’être justes, et qui regardaient tous les autres de haut. Jésus leur dit cette parabole.
fr.R: Certaines personnes étaient sûres d’être bonnes et en règle avec Dieu, et elles se croyaient meilleures que tout le monde. Jésus leur a raconté cette histoire.

sw.R: Watu fulani walikuwa na hakika kwamba wao ni wema na wako sawa mbele ya Mungu. Walijiona bora kuliko watu wengine wote. Yesu akawaambia mfano huu:

decisions.choice: righteous: in the right before God
decisions.reason: The word means just, upright, and so accepted by God. These people trusted their own goodness to make them right with God (16:15).

decisions.choice: looked down on: treated as nothing
decisions.reason: The verb means to count as worthless (23:11).

decisions.choice: good and right with God
decisions.reason: Readable explains the word, as the meaning decision does.

decisions.choice: the people described first, then the parable
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable describe the hearers in one sentence and introduce the parable in another.

decisions.choice: tenían por nada (L); miraban por encima del hombro (B)
decisions.reason: The verb means to treat others as nothing (meaning decision m2). Literal keeps that picture; Balanced uses the everyday Spanish idiom for looking down on people.

decisions.choice: justes (L, B); bonnes et en règle avec Dieu (R)
decisions.reason: The style guide's term for righteous; Readable says "en règle avec Dieu" where the English Readable says "right with God" (m1).

decisions.choice: kuwaona kuwa si kitu (L); kuwaona kuwa duni (B)
decisions.reason: The verb means to treat others as nothing (meaning decision m2). Literal keeps that picture word for word; Balanced says they counted others as lesser.

source.text: Ἄνθρωποι δύο ἀνέβησαν εἰς τὸ ἱερὸν προσεύξασθαι, ὁ εἷς Φαρισαῖος καὶ ὁ ἕτερος τελώνης.

records.literal_gloss: Men two went up into the temple to pray, the one a Pharisee and the other a tax collector.

en.L: "Two men went up into the temple to pray, the one a Pharisee and the other a tax collector.
en.B: "Two men went up to the temple to pray. One was a Pharisee, and the other was a tax collector.
en.R: "Two men went up to the temple courts to pray. One of them was a Pharisee. The other was a man who collected taxes.

es.L: «Subieron dos hombres al templo para orar, el uno fariseo y el otro publicano.
es.B: «Dos hombres subieron al templo a orar. Uno de ellos era fariseo, y el otro, cobrador de impuestos.
es.R: «Dos hombres subieron a los patios del templo para orar. Uno de ellos era fariseo. El otro era un hombre que cobraba impuestos.

fr.L: « Deux hommes sont montés au temple pour prier, l’un Pharisien et l’autre collecteur d’impôts.
fr.B: « Deux hommes sont montés dans la cour du temple pour prier. L’un était Pharisien, et l’autre collecteur d’impôts.
fr.R: « Deux hommes sont montés dans la cour du temple pour prier. L’un d’eux était un Pharisien. L’autre était un collecteur d’impôts.

sw.L: "Watu wawili walipanda hekaluni kuomba, mmoja wao Mfarisayo na yule mwingine mtoza ushuru.
sw.B: "Wanaume wawili walikwenda juu hekaluni kuomba. Mmoja alikuwa Mfarisayo, na mwingine alikuwa mtoza ushuru.
sw.R: "Wanaume wawili walipanda kwenda kwenye viwanja vya hekalu ili kuomba. Mmoja wao alikuwa Mfarisayo. Mwingine alikuwa mtoza ushuru.

decisions.choice: a Pharisee: a member of a Jewish movement devoted to keeping the law of Moses strictly
decisions.reason: As explained at 5:17 and 17:20. Pharisees were respected by the people for their devotion.

decisions.choice: a tax collector: a Jew who collected taxes for the Romans or their rulers
decisions.reason: As at 3:12 and 5:27. Tax collectors were despised as collaborators and cheats.

decisions.choice: went up into the temple: the temple stood on a hill in Jerusalem
alternatives: went up into the sanctuary building
decisions.reason: People went up to the temple and down from it (18:14). Prayer was offered there at the times of the morning and evening sacrifices (Acts 3:1). The word is the temple with its courts, not the sanctuary building.

decisions.choice: the temple courts
decisions.reason: Readable shows that they prayed in the courts, not inside the building.

decisions.choice: the quotation opens here and runs to 18:14
alternatives: no quotation marks for the parable
decisions.reason: Jesus tells the parable and comments on it in one speech.

decisions.choice: fariseo; publicano (L), cobrador de impuestos (B), un hombre que cobraba impuestos (R)
decisions.reason: "Publicano" is the traditional name for these men (meaning decision m2) and Literal keeps it; Balanced and Readable say what they did, as in Luke 3:12. The same through verse 13.

decisions.choice: collecteur d’impôts at every level
alternatives: un homme qui récoltait les impôts (R)
decisions.reason: The style guide's term: "publicain" is a church word few readers understand, and "collecteur d’impôts" is plain enough for Readable too, where the English loosens it to "a man who collected taxes".

decisions.choice: le temple (L); la cour du temple (B, R)
decisions.reason: As the style guide and Luke 2: the word means the whole temple area, and the men prayed in its courts, not in the sanctuary (m3). English Balanced keeps "temple"; French Balanced follows the term sheet.

decisions.choice: mtoza ushuru
decisions.reason: The English Readable says "a man who collected taxes". "Mtoza ushuru" is already plain Swahili for that, so Readable keeps the term used across the New Testament drafts.

source.text: ὁ Φαρισαῖος σταθεὶς πρὸς ἑαυτὸν ταῦτα προσηύχετο· Ὁ θεός, εὐχαριστῶ σοι ὅτι οὐκ εἰμὶ ὥσπερ οἱ λοιποὶ τῶν ἀνθρώπων, ἅρπαγες, ἄδικοι, μοιχοί, ἢ καὶ ὡς οὗτος ὁ τελώνης·

records.literal_gloss: The Pharisee having stood toward himself thus was praying, God, I thank you that not I am like the rest of the men, swindlers, unrighteous, adulterers, or even like this tax collector;

en.L: The Pharisee, standing, was praying these things toward himself: 'God, I thank {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} that I am not like the rest of {{gender:people|men}}, swindlers, unrighteous, adulterers, or even like this tax collector.
en.B: The Pharisee stood and prayed this prayer about himself: 'God, I thank {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} that I am not like the rest of humanity, who are swindlers, crooks and adulterers, or even like this tax collector.
en.R: The Pharisee stood up and prayed about himself. He said, 'God, thank {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} that I am not like other people. They rob others, they do evil, and they are not faithful in marriage. Thank {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} that I am not like this tax collector either.

es.L: El fariseo, de pie, oraba para sí estas cosas: “Dios, {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} agradezco que no soy como el resto de {{gender:la gente|los hombres}}, estafadores, injustos, adúlteros, o incluso como este publicano.
es.B: El fariseo se puso de pie y oró así acerca de sí mismo: “Dios, {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} agradezco no ser como el resto de la humanidad, que son estafadores, tramposos y adúlteros, ni siquiera como ese cobrador de impuestos.
es.R: El fariseo se puso de pie y oró acerca de sí mismo. Dijo: “Dios, {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} agradezco que no soy como las demás personas. Ellas roban a otros, hacen el mal y no son fieles en su matrimonio. Te agradezco que tampoco soy como este cobrador de impuestos.

fr.L: Le Pharisien, se tenant debout, priait ainsi en lui-même : “Ô Dieu, je {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} rends grâce de ce que je ne suis pas comme le reste des {{gender:humains|hommes}}, voleurs, injustes, adultères, ou même comme ce collecteur d’impôts.
fr.B: Le Pharisien s’est tenu debout et il a fait cette prière à son propre sujet : “Ô Dieu, je {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} remercie de ne pas être comme le reste des humains, qui sont voleurs, malhonnêtes et adultères, ou même comme ce collecteur d’impôts.
fr.R: Le Pharisien s’est levé et il a prié en parlant de lui-même. Il a dit : “Ô Dieu, je {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} remercie parce que je ne suis pas comme les autres. Ils volent, ils font le mal et ils trompent leur mari ou leur femme. Je {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} remercie aussi parce que je ne suis pas comme ce collecteur d’impôts.

sw.L: Yule Mfarisayo, akisimama, alikuwa akiomba haya kwa nafsi yake: 'Ee Mungu, nakushukuru kwa sababu sifanani na wanadamu wengine, matapeli, wasio waadilifu, wazinzi, au hata na huyu mtoza ushuru.
sw.B: Mfarisayo alisimama, akaomba hivi juu yake mwenyewe: 'Mungu, nakushukuru kwamba sifanani na wanadamu wengine walio matapeli, wahalifu na wazinzi, wala sifanani na huyu mtoza ushuru.
sw.R: Mfarisayo alisimama, akaomba kuhusu nafsi yake. Akasema, 'Mungu, asante kwamba mimi si kama watu wengine. Wao huwanyang'anya wengine, hutenda maovu, na si waaminifu katika ndoa. Asante kwamba mimi si kama huyu mtoza ushuru pia.

decisions.choice: toward himself: he prayed about himself, or to himself
alternatives: standing by himself, apart from others
decisions.reason: The phrase can go with "praying" (he prayed to himself, or about himself) or with "standing" (he stood by himself). Either way the prayer is centered on himself: "I" comes again and again.

decisions.choice: swindlers, unrighteous, adulterers: people who rob, who do wrong, who are unfaithful in marriage
decisions.reason: The first word means grasping people who take from others. The second means wrongdoers in general.

decisions.choice: I thank you: thanks used as a way to list his own merits
decisions.reason: Thanking God was right (Psalm 100:4), but this prayer asks for nothing and compares himself with others.

decisions.choice: Thank you that I am not like this tax collector either.
alternatives: or even like this tax collector
decisions.reason: Readable repeats the thanks to keep the sentences short.

decisions.choice: the prayer is in single quotation marks inside the parable and runs to 18:12
decisions.reason: The Pharisee's words are quoted inside Jesus' speech.

decisions.choice: para sí (L); acerca de sí mismo (B, R)
decisions.reason: The Greek can mean he prayed about himself or to himself (meaning decision m1, uncertain). "Para sí" in Literal can carry either; Balanced and Readable follow the English reading, "about himself".

decisions.choice: kwa nafsi yake (L); juu yake mwenyewe (B); kuhusu nafsi yake (R)
decisions.reason: The Greek can mean he prayed about himself or to himself (meaning decision m1, uncertain). "Kwa nafsi yake" in Literal can carry either; Balanced and Readable follow the English reading, "about himself".

records.literal_gloss: I fast twice in the week, I tithe all things as many as I gain.

en.L: I fast twice in the week; I give a tenth of all that I gain.'
en.B: Twice every week I fast, and I give a tenth of everything I take in.'
en.R: I go without food two days every week. And I give a tenth of all the money I get.'

es.L: Ayuno dos veces en la semana, pago el diezmo de todo cuanto adquiero”.
es.B: Dos veces por semana ayuno, y entrego la décima parte de todo lo que recibo”.
es.R: Dejo de comer dos días cada semana. Y doy la décima parte de todo el dinero que recibo”.

fr.L: Je jeûne deux fois par semaine, je donne la dîme de tout ce que j’acquiers.”
fr.B: Deux fois par semaine, je jeûne, et je donne le dixième de tout ce que je gagne.”
fr.R: Je ne mange rien deux jours par semaine. Et je donne le dixième de tout l’argent que je reçois.”

sw.L: Ninafunga mara mbili kila wiki; natoa zaka ya kila kitu ninachopata.'
sw.B: Kila wiki ninafunga siku mbili, na ninatoa sehemu ya kumi ya kila kitu ninachopokea.'
sw.R: Ninakaa bila kula siku mbili kila wiki. Na ninatoa sehemu ya kumi ya fedha zote ninazopata.'

decisions.choice: I fast twice a week: going beyond what the law required
decisions.reason: The law of Moses commanded fasting only on the Day of Atonement (Leviticus 16:29). Devout Jews of the time also fasted twice a week, on Mondays and Thursdays.

decisions.choice: I give a tenth of all I gain: the tithe, on everything, not only what the law named
alternatives: a tenth of his profit only
decisions.reason: The law required a tenth of the crops and herds (Deuteronomy 14:22-23). The Pharisees were careful to tithe even small herbs (11:42). This man tithes all he acquires.

decisions.choice: go without food; all the money I get
decisions.reason: Readable explains fasting and puts "gain" in everyday words.

source.text: ὁ δὲ τελώνης μακρόθεν ἑστὼς οὐκ ἤθελεν οὐδὲ τοὺς ὀφθαλμοὺς ἐπᾶραι εἰς τὸν οὐρανόν, ἀλλ’ ἔτυπτε τὸ στῆθος αὐτοῦ λέγων· Ὁ θεός, ἱλάσθητί μοι τῷ ἁμαρτωλῷ.

records.literal_gloss: But the tax collector afar off standing not was willing not even the eyes to lift up to heaven, but was striking the breast of himself saying, God, be merciful to me the sinner.

en.L: But the tax collector, standing far off, was not willing even to lift up [his] eyes to heaven, but was striking his breast, saying, 'God, be merciful to me, the sinner.'
en.B: The tax collector, though, kept back at a distance and would not even lift his eyes toward heaven. Instead he struck his chest again and again and said, 'God, be merciful to me, the sinner!'
en.R: But the tax collector stood far away. He did not even look up toward heaven. He kept beating on his chest in sorrow. He said, 'God, be merciful to me. I am a sinner!'

es.L: Pero el publicano, de pie a lo lejos, no quería levantar ni siquiera los ojos hacia el cielo, sino que se daba golpes en el pecho, diciendo: “Dios, ten misericordia de mí, el pecador”.
es.B: El cobrador de impuestos, en cambio, se quedó a distancia y ni siquiera quería levantar la mirada al cielo. Se golpeaba el pecho una y otra vez y decía: “¡Dios, ten misericordia de mí, el pecador!”.
es.R: Pero el cobrador de impuestos se quedó de pie lejos. Ni siquiera miró hacia el cielo. Se golpeaba el pecho una y otra vez, lleno de tristeza. Decía: “Dios, ten compasión de mí. ¡Soy un pecador!”.

fr.L: Mais le collecteur d’impôts, se tenant à distance, ne voulait même pas lever les yeux vers le ciel, mais il se frappait la poitrine, en disant : “Ô Dieu, sois favorable envers moi, le pécheur.”
fr.B: Le collecteur d’impôts, lui, restait à l’écart et n’osait même pas lever les yeux vers le ciel. Au contraire, il se frappait la poitrine encore et encore, et il disait : “Ô Dieu, fais-moi grâce, à moi, le pécheur !”
fr.R: Mais le collecteur d’impôts, lui, est resté loin. Il n’a même pas levé les yeux vers le ciel. Il se frappait la poitrine parce qu’il était triste de son péché. Il disait : “Ô Dieu, aie pitié de moi. Je suis un pécheur !”

sw.L: Lakini yule mtoza ushuru, akiwa amesimama mbali, hakutaka hata kuinua macho [yake] kuelekea mbinguni, bali alikuwa akijipiga kifua chake, akisema, 'Mungu, nihurumie mimi, yule mwenye dhambi.'
sw.B: Lakini yule mtoza ushuru alibaki amesimama kwa mbali, wala hakutaka hata kutazama juu mbinguni. Badala yake aliendelea kujipiga kifua, akisema, 'Mungu, nihurumie mimi, mwenye dhambi!'
sw.R: Lakini yule mtoza ushuru alisimama mbali. Hakutazama hata juu mbinguni. Aliendelea kujipiga kifua kwa huzuni. Akasema, 'Mungu, nihurumie. Mimi ni mwenye dhambi!'

decisions.choice: be merciful to me: turn your anger away from me and show me mercy
alternatives: have pity on me in general
decisions.reason: This verb is not the usual word for mercy. It is used for God being turned from anger and making peace through the removing of sin (Hebrews 2:17 uses it of atoning for sins). In the temple, at the hour of sacrifice, the man asks God to deal with his sin and accept him.

decisions.choice: the sinner: he sees himself as the sinner, with no one to compare himself to
decisions.reason: The article points to himself alone. Where the Pharisee compared himself with others, the tax collector does not.

decisions.choice: striking his breast: a sign of grief and sorrow for sin
decisions.reason: People beat their chests in deep grief (23:48).

decisions.choice: standing far off, eyes down: shame before God
decisions.reason: People usually prayed standing, looking up toward heaven. He keeps his distance and his eyes down, like Ezra in Ezra 9:6.

decisions.choice: I am a sinner!
decisions.reason: Readable makes the description a sentence of its own.

decisions.choice: in sorrow
decisions.reason: Readable says what the gesture meant.

decisions.choice: ten misericordia de mí (L, B); ten compasión de mí (R)
decisions.reason: The verb asks God to turn his anger away and show mercy (meaning decision m1). "Sé propicio" is the older Bible phrase and is not everyday Spanish; "ten misericordia" says the plea plainly, and Readable uses the plainer "compasión".

decisions.choice: nihurumie
decisions.reason: The verb asks God to turn his anger away and show mercy (meaning decision m1). "Kuhurumia" is the everyday word for showing mercy and suits a plea from a broken man; "kuwia radhi" (to pardon) would say less about mercy.

source.text: λέγω ὑμῖν, κατέβη οὗτος δεδικαιωμένος εἰς τὸν οἶκον αὐτοῦ παρ’ ἐκεῖνον· ὅτι πᾶς ὁ ὑψῶν ἑαυτὸν ταπεινωθήσεται, ὁ δὲ ταπεινῶν ἑαυτὸν ὑψωθήσεται.

records.literal_gloss: I say to you, went down this one justified to the house of him rather than that one; for everyone exalting himself will be humbled, the [one] however humbling himself will be exalted.

en.L: I tell you, this man went down to his house justified rather than that one. For everyone who exalts {{gender:themselves|himself}} will be humbled, but the one who humbles {{gender:themselves|himself}} will be exalted."
en.B: I tell you, it was this man, not the other, who went home put right with God. For everyone who lifts {{gender:themselves|himself}} up will be brought low, and the one who takes the low place will be lifted up."
en.R: I tell you, when the two men went home, God had accepted the tax collector as right with {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, but not the Pharisee. Anyone who puts {{gender:themselves|himself}} above others will be brought down. But anyone who is humble will be lifted up."

es.L: {{plural_you:Les|Os}} digo que este bajó a su casa justificado, y no aquel; porque todo el que se ensalza a sí mismo será humillado, pero el que se humilla a sí mismo será ensalzado».
es.B: {{plural_you:Les|Os}} digo que fue este, y no el otro, quien volvió a su casa justificado ante Dios. Porque todo el que se ensalza será rebajado, y el que ocupa el lugar humilde será ensalzado».
es.R: {{plural_you:Les|Os}} digo que, cuando los dos hombres volvieron a casa, Dios había aceptado al cobrador de impuestos como justo ante {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}, pero no al fariseo. El que se pone por encima de los demás será rebajado. Pero el que es humilde será levantado».

fr.L: Je vous le dis, celui-ci est descendu dans sa maison justifié, plutôt que celui-là. Car quiconque s’élève sera abaissé, mais celui qui s’abaisse sera élevé. »
fr.B: Je vous le dis, c’est cet homme-ci, et non l’autre, qui est rentré chez lui déclaré juste par Dieu. Car quiconque s’élève lui-même sera abaissé, et celui qui prend la dernière place sera élevé. »
fr.R: Je vous le dis : quand les deux hommes sont rentrés chez eux, Dieu avait mis le collecteur d’impôts en règle avec {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}, mais pas le Pharisien. Celui qui se place au-dessus des autres sera abaissé. Mais celui qui est humble sera élevé. »

sw.L: Nawaambia, huyu alishuka kurudi nyumbani kwake akiwa amehesabiwa haki, si yule mwingine; kwa sababu kila mtu anayejiinua atashushwa, lakini yule anayejishusha atainuliwa."
sw.B: Nawaambia, ni huyu, wala si yule mwingine, aliyerudi nyumbani akiwa amekubaliwa na Mungu kuwa mwenye haki. Kwa maana kila anayejiinua atashushwa chini, na anayejinyenyekeza atainuliwa."
sw.R: Nawaambia, wale watu wawili waliporudi nyumbani, Mungu alikuwa amemkubali yule mtoza ushuru kuwa mwenye haki mbele {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}, lakini hakumkubali yule Mfarisayo. Mtu yeyote anayejiweka juu ya wengine atashushwa. Lakini mtu mnyenyekevu atainuliwa."

decisions.choice: justified: declared right with God, accepted by him
decisions.reason: The verb is used for a judge's ruling that someone is in the right. God accepted the man who confessed his sin, not the one who listed his good deeds (compare Romans 4:5).

decisions.choice: rather than that one: the other was not justified
decisions.reason: The phrase does not mean both were justified to different degrees; it means this one and not the other.

decisions.choice: whoever exalts himself will be humbled: God reverses human rank
decisions.reason: Jesus said the same at a meal (14:11). The passives point to God, who brings down the proud and lifts up the lowly (1:52).

decisions.choice: put right with God (B); God had accepted ... as right with him (R)
decisions.reason: "Justified" is church language. Balanced and Readable say what it means; Literal keeps the word.

decisions.choice: brought low ... lifted up (B); brought down ... lifted up (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable use the picture of going down and up.

decisions.choice: se ensalza ... se humilla, with no gender span
decisions.reason: The English has {{gender:themselves|himself}}. The Spanish reflexive "se" serves for a man or a woman, so there is no second wording for the setting to choose; "todo el que" is the ordinary Spanish for "everyone who".

decisions.choice: justifié (L); déclaré juste par Dieu (B); Dieu l’avait mis en règle avec lui (R)
decisions.reason: The style guide's terms for justify. Literal keeps the word; Balanced says what it means, adding "par Dieu" as the English Balanced says "with God"; Readable follows the English "right with him" (m1).

decisions.choice: quiconque s’élève; celui qui s’abaisse, with no gender span
alternatives: a gender setting on the reflexive
decisions.reason: The French reflexive "se" does not mark sex, and "quiconque" and "celui qui" already mean anyone, so French needs no setting where the English has "themselves / himself".

decisions.choice: amehesabiwa haki (L); amekubaliwa na Mungu kuwa mwenye haki (B, R)
decisions.reason: The word means declared right with God and accepted by him (meaning decision m1). Literal uses the standard phrase "kuhesabiwa haki"; Balanced and Readable say what it means, as the English does.

source.text: Προσέφερον δὲ αὐτῷ καὶ τὰ βρέφη ἵνα αὐτῶν ἅπτηται· ἰδόντες δὲ οἱ μαθηταὶ ἐπετίμων αὐτοῖς.

records.literal_gloss: They were bringing then to him also the infants, that them he might touch; having seen however the disciples were rebuking them.

en.L: And they were bringing even the infants to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, so that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} might touch them; but the disciples, having seen [it], were rebuking them.
en.B: People were even bringing their babies to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, so that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} would touch them. The disciples saw it and began to scold them.
en.R: People were bringing even their babies to Jesus. They wanted {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} to touch them. But when the disciples saw this, they told the people to stop.

es.L: Y {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} traían también los bebés para que los tocara; pero los discípulos, al ver[lo], los reprendían.
es.B: La gente {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} traía incluso a sus bebés para que los tocara. Al ver esto, los discípulos comenzaron a reprenderlos.
es.R: La gente llevaba incluso a sus bebés a Jesús. Querían que {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} los tocara. Pero cuando los discípulos vieron esto, les dijeron a esas personas que no lo hicieran.

fr.L: Et on {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} amenait même les nourrissons pour qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} les touche ; mais les disciples, voyant [cela], les réprimandaient.
fr.B: Des gens {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} amenaient même leurs bébés pour qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} les touche. Quand les disciples virent cela, ils se mirent à les rabrouer.
fr.R: Des gens amenaient même leurs bébés à Jésus. Ils voulaient qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} les touche. Mais quand les disciples ont vu cela, ils ont dit aux gens d’arrêter.

sw.L: Na walikuwa wakimletea hata watoto wachanga ili awaguse; lakini wanafunzi, walipoona, walikuwa wakiwakemea.
sw.B: Watu walikuwa wakimletea hata watoto wao wachanga ili awaguse. Wanafunzi walipoona hivyo, wakaanza kuwakemea.
sw.R: Watu walikuwa wakimletea Yesu hata watoto wao wachanga. Walitaka awaguse. Lakini wanafunzi walipoona hivyo, waliwaambia watu hao waache.

decisions.choice: infants: babies
decisions.reason: The word means a newborn or very young child. In 18:16 Jesus calls them little children.

decisions.choice: touch them: lay hands on them in blessing
decisions.reason: Parents brought children to a teacher to be blessed with his touch (compare Mark 10:16; Genesis 48:14).

decisions.choice: were rebuking them: those who brought the children
decisions.reason: The disciples spoke sternly to the people bringing the children, perhaps thinking Jesus had more important work.

decisions.choice: told the people to stop
decisions.reason: Readable says whom the disciples spoke to and what they said.

source.text: ὁ δὲ Ἰησοῦς προσεκαλέσατο αὐτὰ λέγων· Ἄφετε τὰ παιδία ἔρχεσθαι πρός με καὶ μὴ κωλύετε αὐτά, τῶν γὰρ τοιούτων ἐστὶν ἡ βασιλεία τοῦ θεοῦ.

records.literal_gloss: But Jesus called them to [him] saying, Permit the little children to come to me and not do forbid them, for of such is the kingdom of God.

en.L: But Jesus called them to [{{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}], saying, "Allow the little children to come to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, and do not forbid them, for the kingdom of God belongs to such as these.
en.B: But Jesus called them over and said, "Let the little children come to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, and do not try to stop them. The kingdom of God belongs to those who are like them.
en.R: But Jesus called for the children to come to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. He said, "Let the children come to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}! Do not keep them away. The kingdom of God belongs to people who are like them.

es.L: Pero Jesús los llamó [junto a {{deity_pronoun:sí|Sí}}], diciendo: «{{plural_you:Dejen|Dejad}} que los niños vengan a {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}, y no se lo {{plural_you:impidan|impidáis}}, porque de los que son como estos es el reino de Dios.
es.B: Pero Jesús los llamó y dijo: «{{plural_you:Dejen|Dejad}} que los niños pequeños vengan a {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}, y no {{plural_you:traten|tratéis}} de impedírselo. El reino de Dios pertenece a los que son como ellos.
es.R: Pero Jesús llamó a los niños para que vinieran a {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}. Dijo: «¡{{plural_you:Dejen|Dejad}} que los niños vengan a {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}! No los {{plural_you:aparten|apartéis}}. El reino de Dios es de las personas que son como ellos.

fr.L: Mais Jésus les appela [auprès de {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}], en disant : « Laissez les petits enfants venir à {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}, et ne les en empêchez pas, car le royaume de Dieu appartient à leurs pareils.
fr.B: Mais Jésus les fit venir et dit : « Laissez les petits enfants venir à {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}, et n’essayez pas de les en empêcher. Le royaume de Dieu appartient à ceux qui sont comme eux.
fr.R: Mais Jésus a demandé qu’on fasse venir les enfants auprès de {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}. Il a dit : « Laissez les enfants venir vers {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}} ! Ne les écartez pas. Le royaume de Dieu est à ceux qui sont comme eux.

sw.L: Lakini Yesu aliwaita [{{deity_pronoun:kwake|Kwake}}], akisema, "Waruhusuni watoto wadogo kuja {{deity_pronoun:kwangu|Kwangu}}, na msiwakataze, kwa maana ufalme wa Mungu ni mali ya walio kama hawa.
sw.B: Lakini Yesu aliwaita, akasema, "Waacheni watoto wadogo wanijie. Msijaribu kuwazuia. Ufalme wa Mungu ni mali ya watu walio kama wao.
sw.R: Lakini Yesu aliwaita watoto waje {{deity_pronoun:kwake|Kwake}}. Akasema, "Waruhusuni watoto waje {{deity_pronoun:kwangu|Kwangu}}! Msiwafukuze. Ufalme wa Mungu ni wa watu walio kama wao.

decisions.choice: called them: the babies, brought to him by those carrying them
decisions.reason: The word "them" refers back to the infants of 18:15.

decisions.choice: of such is the kingdom of God: the kingdom belongs to people like these
alternatives: the kingdom is made up only of children
decisions.reason: Children had nothing to offer and no standing. The kingdom belongs to those who, like them, come with nothing in their hands.

decisions.choice: the quotation opens here and runs to 18:17
decisions.reason: Jesus' words in 18:16-17 are one saying.

decisions.choice: le royaume de Dieu at every level
decisions.reason: The style guide's term for the New Testament, as in Luke 17 and Mark: the same words at every level, Readable included.

source.text: ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν, ὃς ἂν μὴ δέξηται τὴν βασιλείαν τοῦ θεοῦ ὡς παιδίον, οὐ μὴ εἰσέλθῃ εἰς αὐτήν.

records.literal_gloss: Truly I say to you, whoever not shall receive the kingdom of God as a child, no not shall enter into it.

en.L: Truly I tell you, whoever does not receive the kingdom of God like a child will never enter into it."
en.B: Truly I tell you, anyone who does not welcome the kingdom of God the way a child does will never get into it."
en.R: I tell you the truth, you must accept the kingdom of God the way a child does. If you do not, you will never enter it."

es.L: En verdad {{plural_you:les|os}} digo: el que no reciba el reino de Dios como un niño, de ningún modo entrará en él».
es.B: En verdad {{plural_you:les|os}} digo que quien no acoja el reino de Dios como lo acoge un niño nunca entrará en él».
es.R: {{plural_you:Les|Os}} digo la verdad: hay que recibir el reino de Dios como lo recibe un niño. El que no lo reciba así nunca entrará en él».

fr.L: En vérité, je vous le dis, celui qui ne reçoit pas le royaume de Dieu comme un enfant n’y entrera jamais. »
fr.B: En vérité, je vous le dis, celui qui n’accueille pas le royaume de Dieu à la manière d’un enfant n’y entrera jamais. »
fr.R: Je vous le dis, c’est la vérité : vous devez accueillir le royaume de Dieu comme un enfant l’accueille. Sinon, vous n’y entrerez jamais. »

sw.L: Kweli nawaambia, yeyote ambaye hataupokea ufalme wa Mungu kama mtoto, hakika hataingia ndani yake."
sw.B: Kweli nawaambia, mtu yeyote asiyeukaribisha ufalme wa Mungu jinsi mtoto anavyoukaribisha, hataingia ndani yake kamwe."
sw.R: Nawaambia ukweli, ni lazima mtu aupokee ufalme wa Mungu jinsi mtoto anavyoupokea. Asipoupokea hivyo, hataingia ndani yake kamwe."

decisions.choice: like a child: as a child receives it
decisions.reason: The words could mean receiving the kingdom as one welcomes a child, but the context is about being like children (18:16). A child receives what is given, with trust.

decisions.choice: will never enter: the strongest form of denial
alternatives: will find it hard to enter
decisions.reason: The double negative makes the statement emphatic.

decisions.choice: Truly I tell you (L, B); I tell you the truth (R)
decisions.reason: Luke's usual rendering of Jesus' "amen" (4:24).

decisions.choice: two sentences, addressed to "you"
decisions.reason: Readable puts the condition as a direct instruction.

decisions.choice: En verdad {{plural_you:les|os}} digo (L, B); {{plural_you:Les|Os}} digo la verdad (R)
decisions.reason: The New Testament rendering of the single amen, as in Matthew and Mark. Jesus speaks to the disciples together, so the plural "you" takes the ustedes / vosotros setting. The same in verse 29.

decisions.choice: hay que recibir ... El que no lo reciba así
decisions.reason: The English Readable turns the saying to "you" (English decision r-en-2). In Spanish a "you" here would have to be singular or plural, and either would narrow it; "hay que" and "el que" keep it open to anyone, as the Greek is, and as in Mark 10:15.

decisions.choice: En vérité, je vous le dis (L, B); Je vous le dis, c’est la vérité (R)
decisions.reason: The style guide's form for Jesus's solemn formula, as in Mark 10:15, which has the same saying. Readable puts it in an everyday sentence, as the English Readable does. The same in 18:29.

decisions.choice: Kweli nawaambia (L, B); Nawaambia ukweli (R)
decisions.reason: The New Testament rendering of the single amen, as in Matthew and Mark. The same in verse 29.

decisions.choice: ni lazima mtu aupokee ... Asipoupokea hivyo
decisions.reason: The English Readable turns the saying to "you" (English decision r-en-2). Swahili "you" would have to be singular or plural, and either would narrow it; "mtu" (a person) keeps it open to anyone, as the Greek is, and as in Mark 10:15.

source.text: Καὶ ἐπηρώτησέν τις αὐτὸν ἄρχων λέγων· Διδάσκαλε ἀγαθέ, τί ποιήσας ζωὴν αἰώνιον κληρονομήσω;

records.literal_gloss: And asked a certain him ruler saying, Teacher good, what having done life eternal will I inherit?

en.L: And a certain ruler asked {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, saying, "Good Teacher, by doing what will I inherit eternal life?"
en.B: One of the leaders asked {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "Good Teacher, what do I have to do to inherit eternal life?"
en.R: An important leader asked Jesus, "Good Teacher, what must I do to have eternal life?"

es.L: Y cierto dirigente {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} preguntó, diciendo: «Maestro bueno, ¿haciendo qué heredaré vida eterna?».
es.B: Uno de los dirigentes {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} preguntó: «Maestro bueno, ¿qué tengo que hacer para heredar la vida eterna?».
es.R: Un líder importante preguntó a Jesús: «Maestro bueno, ¿qué debo hacer para tener la vida eterna?».

fr.L: Et un dirigeant {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}interrogea, en disant : « Bon Maître, en faisant quoi hériterai-je de la vie éternelle ? »
fr.B: Un des dirigeants {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} demanda : « Bon Maître, que dois-je faire pour recevoir en héritage la vie éternelle ? »
fr.R: Un dirigeant important a demandé à Jésus : « Bon Maître, qu’est-ce que je dois faire pour avoir la vie éternelle ? »

sw.L: Na kiongozi fulani akamwuliza, akisema, "Mwalimu mwema, nikifanya nini nitaurithi uzima wa milele?"
sw.B: Kiongozi mmoja alimwuliza, "Mwalimu mwema, nifanye nini ili niurithi uzima wa milele?"
sw.R: Kiongozi mmoja mashuhuri alimwuliza Yesu, "Mwalimu mwema, nifanye nini ili nipate uzima wa milele?"

decisions.choice: ruler: a leader, perhaps of a synagogue or of the Jewish council
decisions.reason: The word is used for leaders of a synagogue (8:41) and members of the council (23:13). Luke does not say which. He is rich (18:23), and Matthew 19:20 says he was young.

decisions.choice: Good Teacher: a respectful, even flattering, form of address
alternatives: a statement that Jesus is God
decisions.reason: Jewish teachers were not usually addressed as "good". Jesus' reply (18:19) takes up the word.

decisions.choice: inherit eternal life: receive the life of the age to come
decisions.reason: As in 10:25. Eternal life is the life of the age to come (Daniel 12:2; 18:30).

decisions.choice: have
decisions.reason: As in 10:25: Readable uses a simpler verb; the meaning decision explains "inherit".

decisions.choice: dirigente (L, B); líder importante (R)
decisions.reason: The Greek word is a leader, perhaps of a synagogue or of the Jewish council (meaning decision m1); Luke does not say which. "Dirigente" is a plain word for a leader of a community; "príncipe" now suggests royalty and "principal" as a noun is old-fashioned.

decisions.choice: un dirigeant; Bon Maître at every level
decisions.reason: The man is a leader of some kind (m1): "un chef" sounds like a boss today and "un notable" names a social rank, so "dirigeant" is used. French addresses a teacher of the Law as "Maître", as in Mark 10:17; "Enseignant" would sound like a school.

decisions.choice: kiongozi
decisions.reason: The Greek word is a leader, perhaps of a synagogue or of the Jewish council (meaning decision m1); Luke does not say which. "Kiongozi" is the plain word for a leader of a community; "mtu mkubwa" would mean only an important person.

decisions.choice: uzima wa milele (every level)
decisions.reason: The term used across the New Testament drafts, as in John: "uzima" is life itself, the life of the age to come (meaning decision m3), where "maisha" would be a lifetime or daily living. The same in verse 30.

source.text: εἶπεν δὲ αὐτῷ ὁ Ἰησοῦς· Τί με λέγεις ἀγαθόν;

records.literal_gloss: Said then to him Jesus, Why me call you good?

en.L: And Jesus said to him, "Why do you call {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} good?
en.B: Jesus answered, "Why are you calling {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} good?
en.R: Jesus said to him, "Why do you say that I am good?

es.L: Y Jesús le dijo: «¿Por qué {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} llamas bueno?
es.B: Jesús le respondió: «¿Por qué {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} llamas bueno?
es.R: Jesús le dijo: «¿Por qué dices que yo soy bueno?

fr.L: Et Jésus lui dit : « Pourquoi {{deity_pronoun:m’|M’}}appelles-tu bon ?
fr.B: Jésus répondit : « Pourquoi {{deity_pronoun:m’|M’}}appelles-tu bon ?
fr.R: Jésus lui a dit : « Pourquoi dis-tu que je suis bon ?

sw.L: Naye Yesu akamwambia, "Mbona unaniita mwema?
sw.B: Yesu alijibu, "Kwa nini unaniita mwema?
sw.R: Yesu alimwambia, "Kwa nini unasema kwamba {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}} ni mwema?

decisions.choice: why do you call me good: Jesus makes the man think about what he has said
alternatives: Jesus denies that he is good
decisions.reason: Jesus does not say he is not good. He turns the man's attention to God, the only one who is good, and leaves him to ask what it means to call Jesus good.

decisions.choice: the quotation opens here and runs to 18:20
decisions.reason: Jesus' reply runs on without a break.

source.text: οὐδεὶς ἀγαθὸς εἰ μὴ εἷς ὁ θεός.

records.literal_gloss: No one [is] good except one, God.

en.L: No one [is] good except one: God.
en.B: No one is good but God alone.
en.R: Only God is good. No one else is.

es.L: Nadie [es] bueno sino uno: Dios.
es.B: Nadie es bueno sino solo Dios.
es.R: Solo Dios es bueno. Nadie más lo es.

fr.L: Nul [n’est] bon sinon un seul : Dieu.
fr.B: Personne n’est bon, sinon Dieu seul.
fr.R: Dieu seul est bon. Personne d’autre ne l’est.

sw.L: Hakuna aliye mwema isipokuwa mmoja, Mungu.
sw.B: Hakuna aliye mwema ila Mungu peke yake.
sw.R: Mungu peke yake ndiye mwema. Hakuna mwingine aliye mwema.

decisions.choice: except one, God: an echo of Israel's confession that God is one
decisions.reason: The words recall Deuteronomy 6:4, "the LORD is one". Goodness in the full sense belongs to God (Psalm 106:1).

decisions.choice: God alone
decisions.reason: The word "one" here means only one; Balanced says "alone".

decisions.choice: Only God is good.
alternatives: No one is good except God
decisions.reason: Readable states the positive first.

source.text: τὰς ἐντολὰς οἶδας· Μὴ μοιχεύσῃς, Μὴ φονεύσῃς, Μὴ κλέψῃς, Μὴ ψευδομαρτυρήσῃς, Τίμα τὸν πατέρα σου καὶ τὴν μητέρα.

records.literal_gloss: The commandments you know: Not you shall commit adultery, not you shall murder, not you shall steal, not you shall bear false witness, honor the father of you and the mother.

en.L: You know the commandments: 'Do not commit adultery, do not murder, do not steal, do not bear false witness, honor your father and mother.'"
en.B: You know the commandments: 'Do not commit adultery. Do not murder. Do not steal. Do not give false testimony. Honor your father and your mother.'"
en.R: You know what God's commandments say: 'Do not be unfaithful in marriage. Do not murder. Do not steal. Do not lie about others in court. Honor your father and mother.'"

es.L: Conoces los mandamientos: “No cometas adulterio, no mates, no robes, no des falso testimonio, honra a tu padre y a la madre”».
es.B: Ya conoces los mandamientos: “No cometas adulterio. No mates. No robes. No des falso testimonio. Honra a tu padre y a tu madre”».
es.R: Tú sabes lo que dicen los mandamientos de Dios: “No seas infiel en tu matrimonio. No mates. No robes. No mientas contra otras personas en un juicio. Honra a tu padre y a tu madre”».

fr.L: Tu connais les commandements : “Ne commets pas d’adultère, ne commets pas de meurtre, ne vole pas, ne porte pas de faux témoignage, honore ton père et ta mère.” »
fr.B: Tu connais les commandements : “Ne commets pas d’adultère. Ne commets pas de meurtre. Ne vole pas. Ne fais pas de faux témoignage. Honore ton père et ta mère.” »
fr.R: Tu sais ce que disent les commandements de Dieu : “Ne trompe pas ton mari ou ta femme. Ne tue personne. Ne vole pas. Ne mens pas contre les autres devant un tribunal. Respecte ton père et ta mère.” »

sw.L: Unazijua amri: 'Usizini, usiue, usiibe, usitoe ushahidi wa uongo, waheshimu baba yako na mama.'"
sw.B: Unazijua amri: 'Usizini. Usiue. Usiibe. Usitoe ushahidi wa uongo. Waheshimu baba yako na mama yako.'"
sw.R: Unajua yale ambayo amri za Mungu zinasema: 'Usikose uaminifu katika ndoa. Usiue. Usiibe. Usiseme uongo juu ya wengine mahakamani. Waheshimu baba yako na mama yako.'"

decisions.choice: the commandments: from the Ten Commandments
decisions.reason: Jesus quotes the commandments about one's neighbor from Exodus 20:12-16 and Deuteronomy 5:16-20. Adultery comes before murder, as in some Greek copies of the Old Testament and in Romans 13:9. He does not quote the commandment against coveting, or the commands about God, which the next verses test (18:22).

decisions.choice: bear false witness: give false evidence against someone
decisions.reason: The commandment is about testimony in court (Deuteronomy 19:16-19), though it came to stand for all lying about others.

decisions.choice: do not commit adultery ...: prohibitions
decisions.reason: The form gives commands.

decisions.choice: be unfaithful in marriage; lie about others in court
decisions.reason: Readable explains the two less familiar terms.

decisions.choice: single quotation marks inside Jesus' words; the speech closes here
decisions.reason: Jesus quotes the law inside his speech.

source.text: ὁ δὲ εἶπεν· Ταῦτα πάντα ἐφύλαξα ἐκ νεότητος μου.

records.literal_gloss: And he said, These all have I kept from [the] youth.

en.L: And he said, "All these I have kept from [my] youth."
en.B: The man replied, "I have kept every one of these from my youth."
en.R: The man said, "I have obeyed all these commandments since I was young."

es.L: Y él dijo: «Todo esto lo he guardado desde mi juventud».
es.B: «Todo eso lo he cumplido desde mi juventud», respondió el hombre.
es.R: El hombre dijo: «Yo he obedecido todos esos mandamientos desde que era joven».

fr.L: Et il dit : « Tout cela, je l’ai gardé depuis ma jeunesse. »
fr.B: L’homme répondit : « J’ai observé chacun de ces commandements depuis ma jeunesse. »
fr.R: L’homme a dit : « J’obéis à tous ces commandements depuis que je suis jeune. »

sw.L: Naye akasema, "Haya yote nimeyashika tangu ujana wangu."
sw.B: Yule mtu alijibu, "Nimezishika amri hizi zote tangu ujana wangu."
sw.R: Yule mtu alisema, "Nimezitii amri hizo zote tangu nilipokuwa kijana."

decisions.choice: kept: obeyed, guarded
decisions.reason: The verb means to guard or keep a command. The man means he has lived by them.

decisions.choice: from youth: since he became responsible for keeping the law
decisions.reason: A Jewish boy was taught the law from childhood and held responsible for keeping it as he grew up.

decisions.choice: The man
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the speaker.

source.text: ἀκούσας δὲ ὁ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν αὐτῷ· Ἔτι ἕν σοι λείπει· πάντα ὅσα ἔχεις πώλησον καὶ διάδος πτωχοῖς, καὶ ἕξεις θησαυρὸν ἐν οὐρανοῖς, καὶ δεῦρο ἀκολούθει μοι.

records.literal_gloss: Having heard then Jesus said to him, Yet one thing to you is lacking; all as much as you have sell and distribute to [the] poor, and you will have treasure in [the] heavens, and come follow me.

en.L: And having heard [this], Jesus said to him, "One thing is still lacking for you: sell all that you have and distribute [it] to [the] poor, and you will have treasure in [the] heavens; and come, follow {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}."
en.B: Hearing this, Jesus told him, "You are still missing one thing. Sell all your possessions and hand out the money to the poor. Then you will have treasure in heaven. After that, come and follow {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}."
en.R: When Jesus heard this, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said, "There is one more thing you need to do. Sell everything you own. Give the money to poor people. Then you will have treasure in heaven. After that, come and follow {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}."

es.L: Y al oír[lo], Jesús le dijo: «Todavía te falta una cosa: todo cuanto tienes véndelo y repárte[lo] a [los] pobres, y tendrás un tesoro en [los] cielos; y ven, sígueme».
es.B: Al oír esto, Jesús le dijo: «Todavía te falta una cosa. Vende todo lo que posees y reparte el dinero entre los pobres. Así tendrás un tesoro en el cielo. Después, ven y sígueme».
es.R: Cuando Jesús oyó esto, le dijo: «Hay una cosa más que tienes que hacer. Vende todo lo que tienes. Da el dinero a los pobres. Así tendrás un tesoro en el cielo. Después, ven y sígueme».

fr.L: Et ayant entendu [cela], Jésus lui dit : « Une chose encore te manque : vends tout ce que tu as et distribue[-le] aux pauvres, et tu auras un trésor dans les cieux ; puis viens, suis-{{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}. »
fr.B: En entendant cela, Jésus lui dit : « Il te manque encore une chose. Vends tous tes biens et distribue l’argent aux pauvres. Alors tu auras un trésor dans le ciel. Ensuite, viens et suis-{{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}. »
fr.R: Quand Jésus a entendu cela, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} a dit : « Il te reste encore une chose à faire. Vends tout ce que tu possèdes. Donne l’argent aux pauvres. Alors tu auras un trésor dans le ciel. Ensuite, viens et suis-{{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}. »

sw.L: Naye Yesu aliposikia [hayo], akamwambia, "Bado kitu kimoja kinakupungukia: kila ulicho nacho kiuze, na uwagawanyie maskini, na utakuwa na hazina katika mbingu; na njoo, unifuate."
sw.B: Yesu aliposikia hayo, alimwambia, "Bado unakosa jambo moja. Uza mali yako yote, uwagawie maskini fedha hizo. Ndipo utakuwa na hazina mbinguni. Baada ya hapo, njoo unifuate."
sw.R: Yesu aliposikia hayo, alimwambia, "Kuna jambo moja zaidi unalopaswa kufanya. Uza kila kitu ulicho nacho. Wape maskini fedha hizo. Hapo utakuwa na hazina mbinguni. Baada ya hapo, njoo unifuate."

decisions.choice: one thing is lacking: the man's wealth stands between him and God
alternatives: he must do one more good deed to earn life
decisions.reason: Jesus puts his finger on what the man cannot give up. Following Jesus, not one more deed, is what he lacks (14:33).

decisions.choice: treasure in heaven: riches kept by God, which cannot be lost
decisions.reason: As in 12:33-34. What is given away for God is not lost.

decisions.choice: come, follow me: become my disciple
alternatives: walk behind me for a while
decisions.reason: To follow Jesus is to leave other things and go with him as a disciple (5:11; 9:23).

decisions.choice: hand out the money (B); give the money (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what is given.

source.text: ὁ δὲ ἀκούσας ταῦτα περίλυπος ἐγενήθη, ἦν γὰρ πλούσιος σφόδρα.

records.literal_gloss: And having heard these things very sorrowful he became, he was for rich extremely.

en.L: But having heard these things, he became very sorrowful, for he was extremely rich.
en.B: At these words the man was filled with sorrow, for he was a man of great wealth.
en.R: When the man heard this, he became very sad. He was very rich.

es.L: Pero él, habiendo oído estas cosas, quedó profundamente afligido, pues era rico en extremo.
es.B: Al oír estas palabras, el hombre se llenó de tristeza, porque era dueño de una gran fortuna.
es.R: Cuando el hombre oyó esto, se quedó muy triste. Era muy rico.

fr.L: Mais lui, ayant entendu ces choses, devint très triste, car il était extrêmement riche.
fr.B: À ces mots, l’homme fut rempli de tristesse, car il possédait une très grande fortune.
fr.R: Quand l’homme a entendu cela, il est devenu très triste. Il était très riche.

sw.L: Lakini yeye, akiwa amesikia mambo haya, akawa na huzuni nyingi, kwa sababu alikuwa tajiri kupita kiasi.
sw.B: Yule mtu aliposikia maneno hayo alijawa na huzuni, kwa maana alikuwa na utajiri mwingi.
sw.R: Yule mtu aliposikia hayo, alisikitika sana. Alikuwa tajiri sana.

decisions.choice: for: his wealth is the reason for his sorrow
decisions.reason: Luke explains the man's grief: he had much to give up.

decisions.choice: very sorrowful: deeply grieved
decisions.reason: The word means overwhelmed with grief.

source.text: Ἰδὼν δὲ αὐτὸν ὁ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν· Πῶς δυσκόλως οἱ τὰ χρήματα ἔχοντες εἰς τὴν βασιλείαν τοῦ θεοῦ εἰσπορεύονται·

records.literal_gloss: Having seen then him Jesus said, How difficultly those riches having into the kingdom of God enter;

en.L: And Jesus, having seen him, said, "How hard it is for those who have riches to enter into the kingdom of God!
en.B: Seeing this, Jesus said, "What a hard thing it is for those who have wealth to enter the kingdom of God!
en.R: Jesus saw how sad the man was. He said, "It is very hard for rich people to enter the kingdom of God!

es.L: Y Jesús, viéndolo, dijo: «¡Con qué dificultad entran en el reino de Dios los que poseen riquezas!
es.B: Al ver esto, Jesús dijo: «¡Qué difícil es para los que tienen riquezas entrar en el reino de Dios!
es.R: Jesús vio lo triste que estaba el hombre. Dijo: «¡Qué difícil es para los ricos entrar en el reino de Dios!

fr.L: Et Jésus, l’ayant vu, dit : « Qu’il est difficile à ceux qui ont des richesses d’entrer dans le royaume de Dieu !
fr.B: Voyant cela, Jésus dit : « Qu’il est dur, pour ceux qui ont de la fortune, d’entrer dans le royaume de Dieu !
fr.R: Jésus a vu que l’homme était très triste. Il a dit : « C’est très difficile pour les riches d’entrer dans le royaume de Dieu !

sw.L: Naye Yesu, akimwona, akasema, "Ni kwa shida jinsi gani wale walio na mali wanaingia katika ufalme wa Mungu!
sw.B: Yesu alipoona hivyo, alisema, "Ni jambo gumu kama nini kwa wenye mali kuingia katika ufalme wa Mungu!
sw.R: Yesu aliona jinsi yule mtu alivyokuwa na huzuni. Akasema, "Ni vigumu sana kwa matajiri kuingia katika ufalme wa Mungu!

decisions.choice: having seen him: without "become very sorrowful"
alternatives: having seen that he had become very sorrowful
decisions.reason: Many manuscripts add that Jesus saw he had become very sorrowful, repeating 18:23. Some early manuscripts, including Codex Sinaiticus and Codex Vaticanus, do not have the words, and the SBLGNT follows them. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: how hard it is: riches make it hard to depend on God
decisions.reason: Wealth gives a sense of security that keeps people from depending on God (12:15-21; 16:13). Jesus says it is hard, and 18:27 shows that God can do it.

decisions.choice: how sad the man was
decisions.reason: Readable says what Jesus saw, from 18:23.

decisions.choice: the quotation opens here and runs to 18:25
decisions.reason: Jesus' words in 18:24-25 are one saying.

source.text: εὐκοπώτερον γάρ ἐστιν κάμηλον διὰ τρήματος βελόνης εἰσελθεῖν ἢ πλούσιον εἰς τὴν βασιλείαν τοῦ θεοῦ εἰσελθεῖν.

records.literal_gloss: Easier for it is a camel through an eye of a needle to go than a rich man into the kingdom of God to enter.

en.L: For it is easier for a camel to go through the eye of a needle than for a rich [person] to enter into the kingdom of God."
en.B: In fact, a camel could get through the eye of a needle more easily than a rich person could get into the kingdom of God."
en.R: It would be easier for a camel to go through the tiny hole in a needle than for a rich person to enter the kingdom of God."

es.L: Porque más fácil es que un camello entre por [el] agujero de una aguja que un rico entre en el reino de Dios».
es.B: De hecho, a un camello le sería más fácil pasar por el ojo de una aguja que a una persona rica entrar en el reino de Dios».
es.R: Sería más fácil que un camello pasara por el agujerito de una aguja que una persona rica entrara en el reino de Dios».

fr.L: Car il est plus facile à un chameau d’entrer par le chas d’une aiguille qu’à un riche d’entrer dans le royaume de Dieu. »
fr.B: Oui, il serait plus facile à un chameau de passer par le chas d’une aiguille qu’à un riche d’entrer dans le royaume de Dieu. »
fr.R: Il serait plus facile pour un chameau de passer par le tout petit trou d’une aiguille que pour une personne riche d’entrer dans le royaume de Dieu. »

sw.L: Kwa kuwa ni rahisi zaidi ngamia kuingia kupitia tundu la sindano kuliko mtu tajiri kuingia katika ufalme wa Mungu."
sw.B: Kwa kweli, ngamia angepita katika tundu la sindano kwa urahisi zaidi kuliko mtu tajiri angeingia katika ufalme wa Mungu."
sw.R: Ingekuwa rahisi zaidi kwa ngamia kupita katika kitundu kidogo cha sindano kuliko kwa mtu tajiri kuingia katika ufalme wa Mungu."

decisions.choice: a camel through the eye of a needle: something impossible
alternatives: a narrow gate in a city wall
a rope instead of a camel
decisions.reason: The camel was the largest animal in the land and the eye of a needle the smallest opening. The picture is a deliberate exaggeration; the hearers understood it as impossible (18:26). Nothing in the text supports the idea of a gate called "the eye of a needle".

decisions.choice: needle: a sewing or surgeon's needle
decisions.reason: Luke uses the word for a needle used in medicine, but the meaning is the same.

decisions.choice: the tiny hole in
decisions.reason: Readable explains the eye of a needle.

source.text: Εἶπαν δὲ οἱ ἀκούσαντες· Καὶ τίς δύναται σωθῆναι;

records.literal_gloss: Said then those having heard, Then who is able to be saved?

en.L: And those who heard said, "Then who is able to be saved?"
en.B: Those listening asked, "Then who can be saved?"
en.R: The people who heard this asked, "Then who can be saved?"

es.L: Y los que [lo] oyeron dijeron: «Entonces, ¿quién puede ser salvo?».
es.B: Los que escuchaban preguntaron: «Entonces, ¿quién puede salvarse?».
es.R: La gente que oyó esto preguntó: «Entonces, ¿quién puede ser salvo?».

fr.L: Et ceux qui avaient entendu dirent : « Et qui peut être sauvé ? »
fr.B: Ceux qui écoutaient demandèrent : « Mais alors, qui peut être sauvé ? »
fr.R: Les gens qui avaient entendu cela ont demandé : « Alors, qui peut être sauvé ? »

sw.L: Na wale waliosikia wakasema, "Basi, nani anaweza kuokolewa?"
sw.B: Wale waliokuwa wakisikiliza waliuliza, "Basi ni nani anayeweza kuokolewa?"
sw.R: Watu waliosikia hayo waliuliza, "Basi ni nani anayeweza kuokolewa?"

decisions.choice: be saved: receive eternal life and enter the kingdom
decisions.reason: Here "saved" means the same as inheriting eternal life (18:18) and entering the kingdom of God (18:24-25).
